key: THE men from fire-sticks, with their hands’ swift movement, have, in deep thought, engendered glorious Agni, Far-seen, with pointed flame, Lord of the homestead.
s: Opening a hymn asking Agni for wealth and sons, the verse tells of his kindling; Yāska, Nirukta 5.10, takes the ‘deep thought’ as the fingers, employed in actions, and the fire-sticks as named for the fire resting in them or born of their rubbing.
src: Yāska, Nirukta 5.10, in Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta, translation pp. 78 to 79, archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask (1921)

evidence.words: From two sticks, men with fingers have produced fire by the motion of their hands … Dldhitayah mean fingers: they are employed in (the performance of) actions. Fire-sticks are (so called because) fire rests in them, or because fire is produced from them by attrition. By the motion of their hands, by tlie circular movement of their hands.
evidence.lang: English (Sarup’s translation of Yāska’s Sanskrit; OCR spellings Dldhitayah = Dīdhitayaḥ, tlie = the, kept as printed in the scan text)
evidence.gloss: Yāska quotes 7.1.1 (men with fingers produced fire from two sticks by the motion of their hands) and explains: dīdhitis are fingers, because they are employed in actions; the fire-sticks are so called because fire rests in them, or because fire is produced from them by attrition; by the hands’ motion means their circular movement.
